about.p1: For centuries, the study of anatomy on natural bodies and specimens has been considered the gold standard by professors and students. However, this practice has become increasingly limited, both due to the difficulty of replacing natural anatomical specimens in laboratories, and due to the workload of practical classes dedicated to activities in the anatomy labs.
about.p2: Faced with the need for greater contact between students and anatomical bodies and specimens for better learning, the professors and students of the Departments of Anatomy and Computer Science at the Federal University of Juiz de Fora created an Interactive Anatomy Atlas based on photographs of natural anatomical specimens selected from the Department's collection.
about.p3: The Atlas began to be structured in 2012 by Professors Alice Belleigoli Rezende and Vanessa Neves de Oliveira, the project's originators. Since then, it has gone through several formats and updates, to which many professors and students have contributed. The current version is the result of years of collaborative work aimed at developing a tool that offers students the possibility of seeing and reviewing the specimens in the collection, consolidating the content studied, even outside the laboratories, and that is more suited to the current profile of students.
about.p4: All content can be accessed free of charge and is licensed under Creative Commons (BY-NC-ND 4.0).

guide.p1: First, you must select the system you wish to learn about or study;
guide.p2: Within the system, choose the region or structure to be studied;
guide.p3: Each region or structure has a set of images that correspond in quantity and position to the numbered points below them;
guide.p4: To navigate between images, click on the buttons on the left and right or on the corresponding points;
guide.p5: On the images, blue and red pins will be observed;
guide.p6: The blue pins, when selected, identify the marked structure;
guide.p7: The red pins, when selected, present additional information about the structure in addition to the identification.
